lacker2003.title: Payment System Disruptions and the Federal Reserve Following September 11, 2001
lacker2003.author: Jeffrey M. Lacker
lacker2003.venue: Federal Reserve Bank of Richmond Working Paper 03-16
lacker2003.quote: BoNY's main operations center at 101 Barclay Street, one block north of the World Trade Center, housed the bank's funds transfer and broker/dealer systems, including the bond clearing and settlement systems.
quotes: The two main clearing banks for the government securities market, Bank of New York (BoNY) and J.P. Morgan Chase (JPMC), operated just a few blocks from the World Trade Center.
Both facilities were evacuated on September 11, and operations were established at contingency sites outside the city in New Jersey and New York.
Their headquarters, One Wall Street, was untouched a half a mile from the WTC, but had to be evacuated.
At one point during the week after September 11, BoNY publicly reported to be overdue on $100 billion in payments.
the Federal Reserve at one point injected more than $100 billion in additional liquidity, an unprecedented sum
failures to deliver U.S. government securities rose from $1.7 billion per day the week of September 5 to $190 billion the week ending Wednesday, September 19

Vice Chairman Roger Ferguson was the only member of the Board of Governors in Washington on September 11: Laurence Meyer was in China, Edward Gramlich was in Arizona, Edward Kelley was on vacation, and two seats were vacant.
The second half of the Federal Reserve's two-sentence press release following the attacks was devoted to lending
supports: 101 Barclay Street, one block north of the World Trade Center
clearing banks a few blocks from the WTC
$100 billion of payments overdue at Bank of New York
more than $100 billion of additional Federal Reserve liquidity
Ferguson was the only Board governor in Washington on 11 September 2001
the Federal Reserve's statement that day was two sentences

frb2001.title: Federal Reserve Board press release, September 11, 2001
frb2001.author: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
frb2001.quote: The Federal Reserve System is open and operating. The discount window is available to meet liquidity needs.
supports: the exact two-sentence Federal Reserve statement

draft2002.title: Draft Interagency White Paper on Sound Practices to Strengthen the Resilience of the U.S. Financial System
draft2002.author: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Securities and Exchange Commission
draft2002.venue: Federal Register vol. 67 no. 172, 5 September 2002, pp. 56835-56842 (notice 02-22633; SEC Release No. 34-46432)
draft2002.quote: Should some minimum distance from primary sites be specified for back-up facilities for core clearing and settlement organizations and firms that play significant roles in critical markets (e.g., 200-300 miles between primary and back-up sites)?
quotes: core clearing and settlement organizations generally to set a resumption-time target no later than two hours after the event
establishing remote back-up facilities, in some cases hundreds or even thousands of miles away from the primary site
supports: the draft asked whether to require 200-300 miles of separation

interagency2003.title: Interagency Paper on Sound Practices to Strengthen the Resilience of the U.S. Financial System
interagency2003.author: Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System; Office of the Comptroller of the Currency; Securities and Exchange Commission
interagency2003.venue: dated 7 April 2003, announced by joint press release 8 April 2003, transmitted as the attachment to Federal Reserve supervisory letter SR 03-9 of 28 May 2003
interagency2003.quote: Plans should provide for back-up facilities that are well outside of the current synchronous range that can meet within-the-business-day recovery targets.
quotes: core clearing and settlement organizations should develop the capacity to recover and resume clearing and settlement activities within the business day on which the disruption occurs with the overall goal of achieving recovery and resumption within two hours after an event.
The agencies do not believe it is necessary or appropriate to prescribe specific mileage requirements for geographically dispersed back-up sites.

a recovery-time objective is the amount of time in which a firm aims to recover clearing and settlement activities after a wide-scale disruption with the overall goal of completing material pending transactions on the scheduled settlement date
it is not necessary or appropriate to prescribe any specific technology solution for implementing the sound practices
April 7, 2003
supports: the refusal to prescribe mileage or technology
'well outside of the current synchronous range'
the 'well outside of the current synchronous range' sentence sits under 'Implementation by core clearing and settlement organizations'

ferguson2003.title: September 11, the Federal Reserve, and the Financial System
ferguson2003.author: Roger W. Ferguson, Jr., Vice Chairman, Board of Governors of the Federal Reserve System
ferguson2003.quote: On that morning, sitting in my office in Washington, I watched television with horror as the second plane crashed into the World Trade Center.
quotes: Just before September 11, the number of transfers sent over Fedwire on a normal day was around 430,000, with a total value of $1.6 trillion.
Before September 11, banks held approximately $13 billion in their Fed accounts.
In the days after September 11, these balances ballooned to more than $120 billion because some banks could not move funds out of their accounts.
On September 12, lending to banks through the discount window totaled about $46 billion, more than two hundred times the daily average for the previous month.
On September 11, the number of transfers was down more than 40 percent, with fewer than 250,000 transfers being sent over Fedwire, and the total value was down 25 percent.
supports: Ferguson was in his Washington office that morning
$46 billion of discount window lending on 12 September 2001
bank balances at the Fed rising from about $13 billion to more than $120 billion

unverified: GAO-03-251, 'Potential Terrorist Attacks: Additional Actions Needed to Better Prepare Critical Financial Market Participants' (12 February 2003). gao.gov returned HTTP 403 for the report PDF on 2026-08-22, so nothing from it is used.

That the interagency paper carries SEC Release No. 34-47638. sec.gov returned HTTP 403 on 2026-08-22; the Federal Reserve copy of the paper used here carries no release number, so the number is not claimed.
The dollar cost to individual clearing firms of building out-of-region data centres after 2003 (reported elsewhere as hundreds of millions); no primary source opened.
Whether Roger W. Ferguson Jr. personally authorised the 11 September 2001 press release. His 2003 speech does not say so and no source opened here establishes it.

That the 2003 paper requires back-up facilities outside synchronous range of any firm other than a core clearing and settlement organization. It does not: that sentence appears only under 'Implementation by core clearing and settlement organizations', and the paper states the agencies are not recommending firms move primary sites out of metropolitan locations.

That the interagency paper uses the term 'recovery point objective'. It defines recovery-time objective only; RPO is this book's inference from the synchronous-range requirement, not the paper's wording.

Whether Roger W. Ferguson Jr. watched the second plane strike on television is his own first-person account in the February 2003 Vanderbilt speech; only his presence in Washington as vice chairman is independently corroborated (Lacker 2003, fn. 12).
